payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=autonomous+objective+discovery+multi-objective+reinforcement+learning+Pareto+optimization&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.4673021\", \"title\": [\"Pareto Envelope Augmented with Reinforcement Learning Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach for Large-Scale Constrained Pressurized Water Reactor Optimization\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4673021\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2023]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/springerreference_72504\", \"title\": [\"Multi-objective Optimization: Pareto Optimal Solutions, Properties\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/springerreference_72504\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6310078\", \"title\": [\"Autonomous Portfolio and Derivatives Risk Management AI Agents: Risk-Aware Reinforcement Learning, Multi-Objective Optimization, and Explainable Allocation Decisions\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Recent advances in deep reinforcement learning (DRL), multi-agent systems, and large language model (LLM)-based reasoning have created the technical foundations for autonomous agents that manage portfolio and derivatives risk in real time. Risk-aware DRL methods now incorporate volatility, drawdown, and tail risk constraints directly into the reward or optimization objective, while multiobjective frameworks enable fine-grained control of risk/return trade-offs across diverse investors [Lwele et al., 2025, Deng et al., 2024]. In options and volatility trading, multi-agent architectures that separate the decision to take risk from the policy used to hedge it have been shown to improve risk-adjusted performance relative to traditional or single-agent baselines [Bańka and Chudziak, 2025, Chen et al., 2025]. At the same time, explainable AI (XAI) techniques and sentimentaware tail risk models demonstrate that interpretable drivers of risk can be extracted and communicated to portfolio managers and risk committees [Exp, 2023, Klinkert, 2024]. This paper surveys these developments and proposes a research agenda for autonomous portfolio and derivatives risk management agents that (i) monitor Greeks, volatility regime shifts, and liquidity, (ii) dynamically hedge multi-asset portfolios, and (iii) use scenario-simulation agents to stress test risk, all under a risk-aware, multi-objective, and explainable decision-making framework. We argue that this niche has strong direct capital allocation implications, is rich in deep quantitative structure, and is a natural fit for combining RL with LLM-based reasoning, making it highly relevant to hedge funds and systematic trading desks.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6310078\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.20944/preprints202503.1966.v1\", \"title\": [\"Intelligent Flight Procedure Design: A Reinforcement Learning Approach with Pareto-Based Multi-Objective Optimization\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Current flight procedure design primarily relies on expert experience, lacking a systematic approach to comprehensively balance safety, route simplification, and environmental impact. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning-based method that leverages carefully crafted reward engineering to achieve an optimized flight procedure design, effectively considering safety, route simplicity, and environmental friendliness. To further enhance performance by tackling the low sampling efficiency in the Replay Buffer, we introduce a multi-objective sampling strategy based on the Pareto frontier, integrated with the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method generates executable flight procedures in the BlueSky open-source flight simulator, successfully balancing these three conflicting objectives, while achieving a 28.6% increase in convergence speed and a 4% improvement in comprehensive performance across safety, route simplification, and environmental impact compared to the baseline algorithm. This study offers an efficient and validated solution for the intelligent design of flight procedures.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202503.1966.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 3, 26]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "ae8af700273e6fd5dbcafe6b46c3a5299f2f716ada61bd1d047bbf7fa2f80621", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_objectives", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.4673021", "doi:10.1007/springerreference_72504", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6310078", "doi:10.20944/preprints202503.1966.v1"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4673021", "https://doi.org/10.1007/springerreference_72504", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6310078", "https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202503.1966.v1"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
